newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Shame keeps the poor from soup kitchens.
newsitem.headline: Shame keeps the poor from soup kitchens.

text.p: Around 30,000 people in Serbia and Montenegro get their only warm meals from soup kitchens and a study published on Friday said the number would more than double if people were less shamed by their need.

"At least 75,000 people would be using soup kitchens if they could admit their own poverty," the daily Dnevni Telegraf reported, quoting an Economics Institute study made for International Federation of The Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies and the Yugoslav Red Cross.

Soup kitchens sprang up during the early 1990s when wars in Croatia and Bosnia, U.N. sanctions and the collapse of trade within former Yugoslav sent living standards plummeting. Per capita income shrank from $3,000 in 1990 to $1,500 in 1996.
The study showed that there are almost three million poor in what remains of Yugoslavia.
